task.title: Register a Webhook
task.shortdesc: Subscribe your HTTPS endpoint to receive real-time PayPal event notifications.

ul.li: A publicly accessible HTTPS endpoint (not localhost)
SSL/TLS certificate from a trusted Certificate Authority
A valid Bearer token with webhook management permissions

step.cmd: Send a POST request to create the webhook subscription.
Save the webhook id from the response.
step.stepresult: Store the webhook id — you will need it to verify incoming event signatures.

step.cmd: Implement signature verification in your webhook handler.

info.p: On each incoming webhook POST, verify the signature before processing:
info.codeblock: curl -X POST \ https://api-m.sandbox.paypal.com/v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer A21AAFEpH4PsADbl..." \ -d '{ "transmission_id": "PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-ID header value", "transmission_time": "PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-TIME header value", "cert_url": "PAYPAL-CERT-URL header value", "auth_algo": "PAYPAL-AUTH-ALGO header value", "transmission_sig": "PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-SIG header value", "webhook_id": "5TH26290RN9719702", "webhook_event": { ... event body ... } }'
info.p: A response of "verification_status": "SUCCESS" confirms the event is authentic.

step.cmd: Return HTTP 200 OK from your endpoint after processing.
step.info: PayPal retries delivery up to 5 times with exponential backoff if your endpoint returns a non-200 status or times out (10 second timeout).

result.p: Your webhook is registered. PayPal will POST events to your URL whenever subscribed events occur on your account.

note.p: Use the PayPal Developer Dashboard to send test webhook events to your endpoint without completing a real transaction. Navigate to Webhooks → Simulate.
